slides.title: Guidelines, Policies, Standards, and Procedures
points: Security governance defines how an organization directs and controls security. The exam often tests the difference between high-level guidance, mandatory rules, technical requirements, and step-by-step instructions.

hero.title: Guidelines, Policies, Standards, and Procedures
hero.intro: Security governance defines how an organization directs and controls security. The exam often tests the difference between high-level guidance, mandatory rules, technical requirements, and step-by-step instructions.

blocks.title: Guidelines, Policies, Standards, and Procedures
blocks.prompt: Identify whether the scenario is asking about governance documents, external requirements, governance structure, or accountability for systems and data.

rows: What to do in this situation

blocks.title: Guidelines, Policies, Standards, and Procedures exam shortcuts
items: Example: All sensitive data must be protected.
Example: AES-256 is required for stored restricted data.
Procedures explain exactly how to perform a task.
Example: Follow these seven steps to offboard an employee.
Example: Developers should follow secure coding recommendations.
A playbook is optimized for a specific event or condition.
Example: Ransomware playbook: isolate, notify, preserve, recover.
blocks.example: First decide whether the scenario is about policy direction, a technical requirement, a step-by-step process, external obligations, or ownership/accountability.

questions.q: A document states that all sensitive data must be protected but does not specify exact algorithms or key lengths. What type of governance document is this?
questions.explanation: A policy provides high-level mandatory direction.

questions.q: A document requires AES-256 for restricted data at rest. What type of governance document is this?
questions.explanation: A standard defines a specific mandatory technical requirement.

questions.q: A document gives seven exact steps for offboarding an employee. What type of document is this?
questions.explanation: A procedure explains how to perform a task step by step.

questions.q: A secure coding document recommends preferred practices but allows teams flexibility. What type of governance document is this?
A predefined ransomware response contains scenario-specific actions for isolation, notification, and recovery. What is this?
questions.explanation: A playbook defines actions for a specific operational or security scenario.

questions.q: A company document defines what employees may and may not do with corporate systems and internet access. Which policy is this?
questions.explanation: An AUP defines permitted and prohibited use of organizational resources.

questions.q: A policy requires critical business functions to continue during a major disruption. Which policy is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Business continuity focuses on keeping essential business operations running.

questions.q: A policy defines requirements for restoring servers, applications, and data after a major outage. Which policy is this?
questions.explanation: Disaster recovery focuses on restoring IT systems and data.
